body:
I'd rather not have 5 temp local vectors just to swap underlines, its not that important or performance critical.
I have a new PR that refactors it so it edits the underlines in place instead.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122286

The first point in `temp_underline_points` is never added, since it starts at i=1.

And we could just use `temp_underlines_mesh_points` directly instead of `temp_underline_points` when adding points by keeping track of the last point. Same with color.
Wouldn't it be better to add points directly to a `Vector<Vector2>` instead of copying all of them?

Yea right, that index = 1 was a miss because I changed it back from a previous loop.

Using it directly is what falls into that "some minor gains with the points possible" as you would need to change more in that underline loop and keep track of error cases to not add ghost points to the mesh array. I did not want to touch it to not accidentally break more in what time I had.

With Vector if you dont know the final size to resize so you cant use ptrw() so you are going through the slow CoW gate. Using a LocalVector even with a lot of read-write in-between is a lot faster and does not consume much extra, it just makes the code look more ugly.
Sure, I did not want touch much of the slice and underline logic to not add accidental bugs.

Missed it in the original PR, and it's probably irrelevant for all current use cases (only relevant for bidirectional text), but this is technically wrong. Result of `shaped_text_get_selection` is not necessarily continuous, so merging all of them is not correct, only rects touching each other can be merged.
